edits.rationale: One query answering 'which rows on this page may automation NOT rewrite?' with the guard's own predicate negated — the identical string the 058 DELETE uses — plus a MEMBERSHIP filter (build_status <> 'removed', 0 rows today) stated separately. Exported SQL so a test pins the reuse. Site-wide variant for the discovery check (one query, not one per page).

Pure merge. Pairs each list entry with at most ONE locked row using save_page_sections.matchLockedRow's arms in order (slot exact → slot kebab → component function/name), consume-once; inserts unpaired rows at position-1 clamped to the tail, ascending. Mirroring the guard's arms is what prevents the 189 duplicate-row shape. Returns merged, inserted rows and their indices so the loader can keep section_facts aligned. NormalizeComponentFunction + IsKebabCase move down here; actions.NormalizeComponentFunction becomes a one-line delegate.

After tier assembly and ONLY when a tier served: load + merge; when tier 1 served insert nil into specSectionFacts at each insertedAt (else the len==len guard silently drops the whole fact-scoping payload); report locked_sections_merged/locked_merge_count; best-effort on query failure exactly as loadActiveLockedRows is (Warn, proceed unmerged — the guard still protects the row). Replace the three per-tier cache syncs with ONE after the merge, `sections IS DISTINCT FROM $1::jsonb` (the old text comparison was always true). Header documents source 5 and the no-tier rule. ROUND 2: a skipped merge now leaves a durable agent_error_log trace (bug_historian).

The consumer that compares plan-vs-cache verbatim would file one section_source_drift item per fixed page (13 on day one). Load locked rows once per site (loud on failure — comparing raw lists would flag every locked page) and compare MergeLockedPageSlots(authoritative) vs MergeLockedPageSlots(cache): a locked live section is never drift by itself, a pre-fix cache is not either, a genuine one-store edit still is.

One normaliser for both packages: delegate to datahelpers.NormalizeComponentFunction; ValidateComponentFunction uses datahelpers.IsKebabCase. Same shape as pageComponentAgentWritableSQL → datahelpers.AgentWritableSQLFor. Behaviour unchanged (documented examples pinned in the datahelpers test). ROUND 2 (reuse_agent/architecture): the ROW loader's SQL in save_page_sections is hoisted UNCHANGED to `activeLockedRowsSQL` so a lockstep test can pin that it and the LIST loader (datahelpers.LockedPageSlotsSQL) negate the SAME predicate string; the two loaders stay separate on purpose (ROW vs LIST membership, page_id vs (site,name), import direction) but can no longer drift on the lock test.

plan.risks: ROUND 2 unchanged risks 1–6, 8 from round 1 (below); risk 7 (best-effort skip) is now mitigated by the durable LOCKED_MERGE_SKIPPED row rather than removed — the build still proceeds lock-blind for that one pass by design (the guard protects the row; a fail-loud loader would fail every page build on a transient DB error). New in round 2: (9) hoisting the guard's SQL to a package var touches save_page_sections_action.go — the SQL text is byte-identical and the whole actions suite is green, but it IS a change to the guard file. ---- ROUND 1 RISKS ---- (1) NOT LIVE until the next chassis roll; the acceptance is the owner's five criteria and cannot be run before it — the bug stays OPEN and the chat-box lock stays ON. (2) A merged in-list locked section now draws an `overwrite` lock_blocked_change item per pass instead of a `remove` one (058's design; deduped by item_key) — the fix stops the removal attempts and the lying cache, it does not make locked sections silent; the register entry names the carry-stored-row follow-up as an open question. (3) The merge restores MEMBERSHIP not HISTORY: rows already exiled to the tail by earlier passes stay at the tail until a human moves them or a replan names the component (then the plan position wins via the function arm). (4) The pairing's arm 3 uses component function/name where the guard uses component_id — the list has no ids; if a plan names a component's function while a DIFFERENT locked row renders that component under a positional slot, the merge treats it as present and the guard pairs by identity, which is the same outcome; but two locked rows of one component against a plan naming it once will insert the second — intended, and tested. (5) check_section_source_drift now fails LOUD if the locked-row query errors (previously it had no such dependency) — chosen because the alternative is a silent wave of false drift items. (6) The 'no tier served → no merge' rule leaves a page that has ONLY locked rows and no plan reading 'no sections' — today's behaviour, owned by check_sectionless_pages; stated in the header. (7) Best-effort on the loader's locked query failure means a DB hiccup produces one lock-blind build (Warn logged, guard still protects the row) — the same trade loadActiveLockedRows makes; a reviewer may prefer fail-loud here. (8) NormalizeComponentFunction moved packages; behaviour pinned by test but any caller relying on the old kebabCaseRe var name in actions no longer compiles — grep showed two uses, both updated.
